summary: Jean-Noël Robert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at INALCO and under Bernard Frank, later holding posts at CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (from 1979), and Collège de France as professor (2011–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later holding the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet, and served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

Jeannine Auboyer worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at École du Louvre, EPHE, University of Paris, and under Philippe Stern and Paul Pelliot, later serving at the Guimet Museum (1936; 1965–1980) and CNRS (~1952–1977).

Jeff Dolven studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University. He held positions at Harvard University (~1995–1998), Brandeis University (~1998–1999), and Princeton University, where he became a professor of English (~1999).

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. His career includes posts at Murdoch University (~1992–1999) and the University of Tasmania, where he became professor in 1999.
Jeff Shore works in the fields of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1991 to 2019, later becoming professor emeritus.
Jeff Watt specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under Taitetsu Unno and Myosei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, joining Elizabethtown College as associate professor of religion and Asian studies in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White, later holding posts at UC Berkeley (2001–2002) and Marshall University (assistant professor from 2002).
Jeffrey Davis Schoening works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington, where he studied under Collett Cox and Sanghasena Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, completing his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison before serving as a professor at the University of Virginia (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago, later holding the J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (~2002).

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University and Leiden University under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held faculty posts at Yale University (~1968–1970), Cornell University (~1970–1973), Johns Hopkins University (~1974–1983), and Boston University (from ~1983) as professor of French literature.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, later teaching at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and serving as professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (~1992–1996) and the University of British Columbia (~2003–2009), and held a post at the University of Winnipeg (~2011).
Jeffrey S. Lidke specializes in religious studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at the University of Virginia (visiting assistant professor of religion, attested 2003) and Berry College.
